profileText: a Delegate from New York; born in Tappan, Rockland County, N.Y., September 28, 1739; attended school in New York City; studied law; admitted to the bar and practiced in New York City and Rockland County; Delegate to the First Continental Congress, 1774; judge of Orange County in 1774, 1775, and 1778-1788; member of the provincial convention of April 1775 and of the four New York provincial congresses, 1775-1777, serving as president pro tempore of the second and third provincial congresses; served in the New York state senate, 1781-1789; member of the council of appointment in 1781 and 1782; member of the New York state board of regents in 1784; Delegate to the Confederation Congress, 1785-1787; member of the New York state convention in 1788 to consider the Federal Constitution and voted to reject it; member of the New York state assembly in 1806; died in Blauveltville, Rockland County, N.Y., April 1, 1809; interment in Tappan Church Cemetery, Tappan, N.Y.
